incidents-bot: Pager: KV-cache memory anomaly detected on hosted-runtime-east-1 (shard s-213). OOMs observed, starting ~1708804280. Paging kvcache-oncall.

kvcache-oncall: I'm on it — looking at graphs now. Mem climb started ~1708804280, sustained. Prefetch queue and pagewalk ops spiking.

maya (runtime): I can see the culprit sessions: several very long prompts (>100k tokens) getting continuously batched; KV cache grows superlinearly because prefix reuse + no session cap.

leo (sre): Any evidence of customer impact?

tess (customer-success): Support alert: AcmeCorp reporting 500s on /v1/chat/completions, began ~11:05 UTC. Multiple customers might be affected.

kvcache-oncall: Triage summary: prefetch amplification -> eviction backlog -> GC thrash -> OOM. Short-term mitigation plan: throttle prefetch, cap session KV entries, tighten batch window.

maya (runtime): Hotfix ready. Proposed config changes for shard s-213: reduce `kv.prefetch.depth` 128 -> 8, set `session.max_kv_entries` = 8, and `batch.window_ms` 20 -> 8. Low-risk config patch.

leo (sre): Roll plan? Canary first.

maya (runtime): Deploying to canary (10%):
```
PATCH /api/v1/runtime/configs/s-213
{
  "kv.prefetch.depth": 8,
  "session.max_kv_entries": 8,
  "batch.window_ms": 8
}
```

maya (runtime): Canary metrics: memory per-pod down ~30% within 90s, prefetch ops reduced, no new OOMs on canary.

kvcache-oncall: Rolling to 50% now -> monitoring.

incidents-bot: Deploy status: canary -> 100% success for s-213. No failed hosts.

leo (sre): Observability update: error rate for hosted/text-gen dropped from 6.2% -> 1.1%. P99 latency increased ~30ms due to smaller batching but within SLO.

tess (customer-success): Notified AcmeCorp about mitigation and temporary ETA. They'll watch, asked for logs.

maya (runtime): Followups: 1) Add alert for `session_kv_entries > 64`. 2) Add TTL safeguard for KV entries (30m). 3) Create post-mortem and assign INF-2389.

kvcache-oncall: Handoff in 30m to @leo. Summary for next oncall: root cause = extreme prompt length + continuous batching -> prefetch amplification; mitigation = throttle prefetch + session cap + tighter batch window rolled to all hosts; customer impact ~5% of requests, AcmeCorp among affected.

leo (sre): Acknowledge takeover. I'll keep retention/rate buckets under observation, and have rollback plan to revert batch.window_ms if latency regression worsens.

tess (customer-success): I'll push a status page update and follow up with AcmeCorp. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: Incident state -> mitigated at 1708804689. Post-mortem required.
